metadata.title: Survey of Adult Skills 2023 Data Analysis Manual

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The manual describes the Survey of Adult Skills (PIAAC) as a household survey with a complex sampling design and provides guidance on how to conduct analyses that correctly reflect that design. It explicitly introduces replicate-weight methodology (Balanced Repeated Replication, BRR) and jackknife (JK) as tools for variance estimation, indicating that users should apply the provided survey weights and replicate weights when producing standard errors and confidence intervals. For skill proficiency measures, it also explains how to derive correct inferences when working with the PIAAC skill measures (including WLE scores and the use of plausible values where applicable). Because this document is a data analysis manual rather than an empirical ML study, it does not specify a single analytic weight variable name or whether weights are applied in a particular model run; instead, it instructs analysts to use the weights supplied in the PIAAC datasets and to follow the manual’s procedures for scaling and inference.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a technical data analysis manual that provides procedures for analysing PIAAC microdata rather than reporting an empirical predictive model with a documented missing-data strategy. While it discusses scoring and comparability issues (e.g., WLE availability rules across cycles), it does not present a specific study-level missing-data handling method for an ML outcome. Therefore, missing-data handling is not reported in the sense required for an empirical extraction (no single imputation/deletion rule is tied to a reported model).

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The manual guides researchers in analysing microdata from the second cycle of the Survey of Adult Skills (2022/2023) collected in 31 participating countries/economies. It does not provide a single analytic sample definition (e.g., grade/age subsample, task completion filter, or exclusion rule) because it is a general-purpose analysis guide; instead, it instructs users to apply the complex survey design and to follow the scoring and inference procedures for the relevant skill measures and derived scales.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD technical manual explains how to analyse microdata from the Survey of Adult Skills (PIAAC) Cycle 2 (2022/2023) for adults aged 16–65 across 31 participating countries/economies. It describes the survey instruments (background questionnaire and direct assessment of literacy, numeracy, and adaptive problem solving), the availability of doorstep interviews for language-barrier cases, and the structure of the international database and public-use files. A central focus is correct inference under the complex survey design, including how to use sampling/replicate weights (e.g., BRR and jackknife) and how to work with PIAAC skill measures (including WLE scoring and cycle comparability considerations). The manual also highlights scale comparability issues between PIAAC cycles (e.g., changes in section content and WLE assignment rules when fewer than three valid responses are available), warning that comparing average scores across cycles may require harmonisation steps. As a methodological guide, it does not report model performance metrics or predictive effects from a specific ML analysis.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a framework/methodology document (a data analysis manual) rather than an empirical study that trains and evaluates ML models on a defined analytic sample. Consequently, it does not report a single total sample size, per-country analytic Ns, or a specific set of predictive targets with performance metrics. The extraction therefore leaves empirical ML fields empty and focuses on the documented survey design and scoring/inference guidance.
